title: lll 1.0 landing page: choose the structure
question: The look stays: ember orange, instrument-panel dark, Inter. The roll dealt three page structures for 'many agents, many machines, many harnesses, one board'. Lock one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Two doors, one board
options.thesis: Host it on your laptop or online; every agent, anywhere, lands on the same live board.
materials: orange band split by a hairline seam
options.viewport: Hero split into two doors, left 'on your machine: lll up' on orange, right 'online: one binary and a volume' on dark; both feed down into one real board screenshot, with Claude Code, Codex, pi, opencode and CI chips arriving from either side.
options.risk: The hosting choice can read as a fork in the product rather than two routes to one thing.

options.label: The proof ledger
options.thesis: Lead with how lll was tested: fresh agents, real tasks, judged on the server's own state.
materials: ledger table with drawn state icons
options.viewport: Headline over a 20-row ledger of use cases, each with 10 worker dots in the board's own state colours and a pass mark; the board screenshot sits beside it labelled 'judged here'; install and lll up are one line under the headline.
options.risk: Proof before promise: a visitor who doesn't yet care about agents may not read past the table.

options.label: The event stream
options.thesis: The page is an lll watch stream: agents on different machines and harnesses act, the board answers live.
options.viewport: Full-width split: left a terminal plays back events (codex on ci-runner claims ENG-12, claude-code on a laptop comments, pi on a homelab hands off), right the board moves the same cards in step; the orange band carries the headline above.
options.risk: Motion carries the story, so the static and reduced-motion versions must make the same point on their own.
